extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners preparing or reviewing electronic appendices (sequence listings, computer program listings, large tables) for U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_short: submitting electronic appendices for patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/format requirements for submitting sequence listings, computer program listings, and large tables as electronic files (via EFS-Web or compact disc) and for how they must be incorporated into the specification and handled by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling of replacement compact discs
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a replacement compact disc, the compact disc and copy must be labeled 'COPY 1 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' (with month, day and year of creation indicated) and 'COPY 2 REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY', respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exact replacement label format with creation date. Use same labeling convention for duplicate sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification incorporation-by-reference for compact discs/text files
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must contain an incorporation-by-reference of the material on the compact disc (or text file) in a separate paragraph (§ 1.77(b)(5)), identifying each compact disc by the names of the files contained on each of the compact discs, their date of creation and their sizes in bytes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may require applicant to amend the specification to include in the paper portion any part of the specification previously submitted on compact disc. Use the separate paragraph to make clear the application as originally filed includes material on the disc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory information to appear on compact disc labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Each compact disc must be labeled with: (i) the name of each inventor (if known); (ii) title of the invention; (iii) the docket number, or application number if known; (iv) a creation date of the compact disc; (v) if multiple discs, label shall indicate their order (e.g., '1 of X'); and (vi) an indication that the disc is 'Copy 1' or 'Copy 2' of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete label info so OPAP and the public can identify and interpret disc contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability, format, and virus-free requirement for files
rubrics_metrics.description: If a file is unreadable on both copies of the disc, the unreadable file will be treated as not having been submitted. A file is unreadable if it is of a format that does not comply with requirements, corrupted by a computer virus, or written onto a defective compact disc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure files comply with required formats (ASCII, specified encodings), are virus-free, and discs are not defective. OPAP will check for viruses, readability, and non-ASCII files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion and counting rules for application size fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sequence listing in an electronic medium in compliance with §§ 1.52(e) and 1.821(c) or (e), and any computer program listing filed in an electronic medium in compliance with §§ 1.52(e) and 1.96, will be excluded when determining the application size fee required by § 1.16(s) or § 1.492(j). For applications where specification/drawings (excluding sequence listings and computer program listings) are submitted on an electronic medium other than the Office electronic filing system, each three kilobytes of content submitted on an electronic medium shall be counted as a sheet of paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings and program listings submitted via EFS-Web as compliant ASCII text are excluded for fee computation; for other electronic submissions count 3 KB = 1 sheet. Tables submitted as ASCII text files via EFS-Web: each three kilobytes counts as a sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and arrangement of application elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the application, if applicable, should appear in the following order: (1) Utility application transmittal form; (2) Fee transmittal form; (3) Application data sheet (§ 1.76); (4) Specification; (5) Drawings; (6) The inventor's oath or declaration. The specification should include sections in order: title; cross-reference to related applications; statement regarding federally sponsored research or development; names of parties to a joint research agreement; statement regarding prior disclosures by the inventor; background; brief summary; brief description of views of the drawing; detailed description; claims; abstract; sequence listing (if on paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 CFR 1.77 ordering. Precede specification section text with uppercase section headings without underlining or bold (see § 1.77(b) & (c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Text-file submission requirements via EFS-Web (.txt/ASCII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text files submitted via EFS-Web must be in compliance with ASCII and have a file name with a '.txt' extension. The specification must contain an incorporation-by-reference paragraph identifying the name of the ASCII text file, the date of creation, and the size of the ASCII text file in bytes similar to 37 CFR 1.52(e)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirements of 37 CFR 1.52(e)(3)-(6) for compact discs are not applicable to text files submitted via EFS-Web, but the ASCII and identification requirements still apply. Use form paragraphs 6.61.02 and 6.71.02 to indicate need to add/amend incorporation statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing submission preferences and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that a sequence listing be submitted in an ASCII text file via EFS-Web rather than in a PDF file. If a sequence listing text file submitted via EFS-Web on the filing date complies with the requirements and applicant has not filed a sequence listing in a PDF file (or on paper) on the same day, the text file will serve both as the paper copy required by 37 CFR 1.821(c) and the computer readable form required by 37 CFR 1.821(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PDF and an ASCII text file are both filed on the same day, a statement that their contents are identical is required. When submitting amendments or replacements via EFS-Web, include statements that no new matter is introduced and indicate support for the amendment in the application as filed (see 37 CFR 1.825).

rubrics_metrics.name: Size limits for text files submitted via EFS-Web
rubrics_metrics.description: One hundred (100) megabytes is the size limit for sequence listing text files submitted via EFS-Web; for all other text file types, 25 megabytes is the size limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a file exceeds these limits, it is recommended to submit the electronic copy on compact disc via Priority Mail Express® from the USPS or by hand delivery on the date of the corresponding EFS-Web filing so it will be considered part of the application as filed. See EFS-Web Legal Framework for additional limits on number/size of files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable compact disc media and file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: A compact disc submitted under 37 CFR 1.52(e) must either be a CD-ROM or a CD-R. CD-RW media (erasable/rewriteable) are not acceptable. The files stored on the compact disc must contain only ASCII characters; no non-ASCII characters or proprietary file formats are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CD-ROM or CD-R to ensure longevity/integrity. A text viewer is recommended for viewing ASCII files. Avoid proprietary formats (e.g., Word, Excel) or embedded non-ASCII characters; OPAP will object to non-ASCII or proprietary formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate compact disc submission and Office processing
rubrics_metrics.description: All compact discs must be submitted in duplicate labeled as 'copy 1' and 'copy 2'. If more than one disc is required, each disc must be submitted in duplicate to form two sets. Both copies should be routed to OPAP; OPAP will check for viruses, readability, non-ASCII files, and compliance with labeling. OPAP will retain one copy and place the other in an artifact folder associated with the Image File Wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a complete set of files is not present on both copies, OPAP will retain the originally filed discs and notify applicant to submit an additional complete copy. For provisional applications, OPAP will notify applicant and require correction where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement/Amendment of compact discs must include all files and update specification
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to the material on a compact disc must be done by submitting a replacement compact disc with the amended file(s) or by filing the material as text files via EFS-Web. A replacement compact disc containing amended files must contain all of the files of the original compact disc that were not amended, and the amendment should include a corresponding amendment to the description of the incorporation-by-reference portion of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the Office, printer, and public can access all current files by referencing only the latest electronic version. Replacement discs missing unamended files will be objected to (¶ 6.72.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing length and placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a computer program listing is 300 lines or fewer (each line ≤72 characters), it may be submitted either as drawings or as part of the specification. Any listing having more than 60 lines submitted as part of the specification must be positioned at the end of the description but before the claims. A listing of more than 300 lines must be submitted as an appendix (ASCII text via EFS-Web or on compact disc) and will not be printed in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted as drawings follow § 1.84. If submitted in the specification, follow § 1.52. Any amendment to a listing in the specification must be made by substitute sheet. Use form paragraphs 6.64.01 and 6.64.02 to notify applicants of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program listing appendix technical specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'computer program listing appendix' submitted on compact disc must comply with § 1.52(e) and the following: (i) Computer Compatibility: IBM PC/XT/AT or compatibles, or Apple Macintosh; (ii) Operating System Compatibility: MS-DOS, MS-Windows, Unix, or Macintosh; (iii) Line Terminator: ASCII Carriage Return plus ASCII Line Feed; (iv) Control Codes: data must not be dependent on control characters or codes not defined in the ASCII character set; (v) Compression: uncompressed data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple listings for a single application may be on one disc; separate discs are required per application. The appendix will not be part of the printed patent; the specification must include a reference to the appendix at the location indicated in § 1.77(b)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and submission rules for large tables and formulae
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables submitted in electronic form (§§ 1.96(c) and 1.821(c)) must maintain the spatial relationships (alignment of columns and rows) of the table elements when displayed so as to visually preserve the relational information they convey. Chemical and mathematical formulae must be encoded to maintain the proper positioning of their characters when displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When lengthy tables are submitted electronically, ensure encoding/presentation preserves alignment and positioning; treat each long table as a separate text file and file names should indicate which table is contained therein. If tables are submitted as ASCII text files via EFS-Web, each 3 KB counts as a sheet for application size fee purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited formats and examiner objection practice (form paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP provides specific form paragraphs to object and require correction for common defects in electronic appendix submissions: missing statement that CDs are identical, missing listings in transmittal letter, specification lacking list of compact discs/files, lack of incorporation-by-reference statement, non-ASCII file formats, unreadable discs, discs containing viruses, missing files on substituted discs, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review and address the specific defects identified by the applicable form paragraph (e.g., ¶ 6.60.01, ¶ 6.61.02, ¶ 6.72.02, ¶ 6.72.03, ¶ 6.72.04, ¶ 6.72.05) and provide the required corrections (resubmit in ASCII, supply duplicate discs, amend specification, provide statements that no new matter is introduced, etc.).
